name: The Hay Adams
insider_take: Where power meets elegance in the shadow of the White House—this is Washington's most prestigious address.
whats_special: Built in 1928 on the former sites of homes belonging to John Hay (Lincoln's private secretary) and Henry Adams (great-grandson of President John Adams), The Hay Adams offers unparalleled views of the White House from its upper floors. The hotel's Off The Record bar is legendary among Washington insiders as a discreet meeting spot for politicians and power brokers. The rooftop has been used as a strategic vantage point by the Secret Service during presidential events.
pro_tip: Book a room on floors 7-8 facing south for the best White House views, especially stunning during the evening when the presidential residence is illuminated. Request these coveted rooms well in advance as they're highly sought after.
dont_miss: The hotel's afternoon tea service in the stunning lobby with its soaring ceilings and Italian Renaissance décor. Walk across Lafayette Square to the White House for photos, then explore the nearby Renwick Gallery and Blair House. The hotel's proximity to the Treasury Building and St. John's Church (known as the "Church of Presidents") makes it perfect for historic walking tours.
pros: Prime location directly across from the White House
Historic elegance with refined luxury accommodations
Exceptional personalized service and attention to detail
Award-winning dining at The Lafayette Restaurant
cons: Historic building may have smaller room sizes
